items.english: "You naughty thing." The young father gazed at the small round arms, and at the child's long, dark-lashed eyes moving busily and sharply without a pause, as if wondering what was to be done, and then with a smile filling his whole face, pinching the child's round thrust-out cheek lightly with his fingers, he felt under the table for a large bowl and put it into her little hands.
notes: 彼女の手 here is the baby's hands, not the mother's; rendered as "her little hands" to keep the reference clear.

items.english: She served the rice, just cooked and hot from the pot with white steam rising thick, and handed it to him. And her young large eyes too, full of a mother's gladness, gazed at the child, never still for an instant, lovely as a little bird. And as if she could bear it no longer, murmuring under her breath, whatever shall we do with this child, looking for all the world helplessly fond, she said, "Baby," firmly, but the smile overflowed her face, and she looked at the man as if asking for help. And the three laughed together, as if they had forgotten everything, as if wondering what to do for the child. And for the child they fell to their meal, with a warm bustle and with laughter and gladness welling up of themselves. And for all their clattering noise they did not hear the sound of the rain and wind.
notes: 坊や is literally a word for 'boy,' though the child was introduced as a girl in p2; both parents use it as baby-talk address. Rendered here as neutral "Baby" to preserve the fork without deciding it in English.

items.english: The young father kept his big red hand spread busily over the table. And holding back the smile the child made well up in him in spite of himself, he steadied the child and put a little food into her small red mouth. In the gaps, hastily opening his own wide mouth, he thrust rice into it.

data.say: Drafted p7 to p9 keeping the long meal-breath and smile words together.
